descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · UAT OAT-06 closing line; TFA-94514 Analytics Access · “queryable via Vikram's existing Convex dashboard access, with clearly named fields and no new UI needed”.

Approach · OAT-06 Measuring How the Pilot Is Working (Usage Analytics) · S23 Vikram's Convex dashboard on the UAT deployment: the same rows, filtered and read without help

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U12 Everything above fires correctly and is queryable through Vikram's existing Convex dashboard access, with clearly named fields (not an unlabeled boolean or an internal enum only a dev would recognize … (UAT OAT-06 closing line; TFA-94514 AC 8; TFA-94609 AC 5; TFA-94609 AC 6)
  • U7 Per physician per day: notes generated, handoffs sent, and time from Pre-Round opened to note complete are aggregated and queryable in Convex (UAT OAT-06 Test 6; TFA-94514 AC 6)
  • T1 Engineering prepares a simple hand-off doc so Vikram knows how to access the analytics data (TFA-94514 AC 9)

Test design technique: Happy path (happy-path) — Walk the normal flow exactly as the UAT / ticket words it; everything it names has to show up.

Given The UAT (deployed) build after a QA physician has done S01, S07 and S15's steps; Vikram's or Tim's existing dashboard access

When Open Data -> pilotDailyRounding, filter userId and day; open pilotUsageEvents, patientActivityEvents, surveyResponses; follow the hand-off doc

Then Every event from the steps is there with the same values as the local run; notes generated, handoffs sent and the open-to-complete time for that physician and day can be read and the average worked out from the doc; no new UI or endpoint was needed

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT OAT-06 closing line; the reader confirms in writing. Done by Tim/Vikram, never by this agent (dev is out of bounds); Q12. An @roundai.test account only, never the store-review account; owner Tim

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method CONFIG · Config check; lane planned in the matrix: manual (manual)

S23 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-06.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20 re-run), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: CONFIG · Config check; secondary: EXPLORATORY · Exploratory testing — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on dev; Source: newspec-c.

UAT item: OAT-06 Measuring How the Pilot Is Working (Usage Analytics) · Section: B · Operational Acceptance Tests · Scenario: OAT-06/S23

Vikram's Convex dashboard on the UAT deployment: the same rows, filtered and read without help

Tickets: TFA-94514 Analytics tracking (ready for qa); TFA-94609 Pilot Surveys (ready for qa)

New local lane newspec-c: status blocked in newspec-c/results.json → blocked (blocked).

Detail:

Not run by this agent, by design: the case is the pilot team (Vikram, or Tim for him) reading pilotDailyRounding, pilotUsageEvents, patientActivityEvents and surveyResponses in the Convex dashboard of the deployed UAT build with their own dashboard access, and confirming in writing (Q12). The QA agent has no dashboard or admin access on dev; its dev reads are account-scoped queries only (the dev results hold one: the QA account's survey record, nothing written). On 43c38a4f the case also lost the guide it says to follow: #86's last commit (43c38a4f) deleted docs/pilot-analytics.md, and no other file in the repo names the analytics tables (S22), so 'the average worked out from the doc' has no doc. The same rows are checked locally with the admin key: S07 (handoff rows, follow-up answers), S13 / S14 (baseline, 4 PM feedback, task-reminder answers and every Not now), S15 (Settings feedback).

Evidence: 1 attached.

Dev run: skipped: not runnable on dev — not-runnable-on-dev: outside-runner (manual: needs-dev-or-prod). This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
